title: Freezing and Anoxic Episodes Induce Distinct Epigenetic Modification Patterns in the Stress-Tolerant Marine Gastropod, Littorina littorea
content: Background/Objectives: The common periwinkle, Littorina littorea, is a marine gastropod that routinely experiences environmental stresses characteristic of intertidal habitats, including prolonged anoxia and freezing. Survival under these conditions depends on metabolic rate depression (MRD), a reversible suppression of energetically demanding cellular processes for energy conservation. Although the metabolic adaptations underlying MRD in periwinkles are well studied, the potential involvement of histone post-translational modifications remains largely unexplored. Methods: In the present study, we investigate the abundance of three core histones and 17 histone modifications in periwinkle hepatopancreas following 24 h exposure to anoxia or freezing using western immunoblotting. Results: Compared with aerobic controls, anoxia significantly increased H3K4me1, H3K9me2, and H3K27me1 abundance, whereas freezing significantly reduced H3K9ac, H3K4me2, H3K9me2, and H3K9me3 abundance. Notably, five histone modifications (H3K4me1, H3K9me2, H3K9me3, H3K27me1, H3K18ac) specifically exhibited statistically significant differences between anoxia and freezing. No significant changes were observed in total core histone abundance, histone arginine methylation, or H3S10 phosphorylation. Conclusions: Overall, these findings identify distinct, stress-associated patterns of histone modification abundance in periwinkle hepatopancreas. Such differences may reflect the distinct physiological challenges imposed by anoxia and freezing. The present study provides a foundation for future investigations into the functional significance of these histone modifications in chromatin regulation and MRD in periwinkles.
